label: copy phase (from 2nd copied output on): fed-back input is v/w/s/e/t/u
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase (t > L), and essentially only once at least one copied token has been fed back (recall_idx >= 2 holds ~98% of the mass; it never fires during the original phase or at <DEL>, and only weakly at recall_idx 1). It also never fires when the input is the first occurrence of that token (in_first=0 for all activations), which follows from copy-phase inputs being repeats. Within the copy phase it is strongly selective for the identity of the fed-back input token: v (26% rate), w, s, e (~19-24%), then t and u (~12%), with a long tail (j, c, k, ...). The strongest activations are on v/w/e fed back at recall_idx 2 in short sequences (e.g. f w c <DEL> f [w]). Rates are a bit higher near the end of the copy (to_go 0-2) and in sequences with few digits, but adding those conditions did not raise F1. The predicate (copy phase, recall_idx >= 2, input in {v,w,s,e,t,u}) gets dev F1 0.56 with mass recall 0.75. Precision is only about 0.48 because the same tokens often fail to activate it, and about 25% of the mass comes from other letters, so the token weighting is graded, not a clean set.
